faqs.question: The AR-1 will not turn on at all. What do I check?
faqs.answer: Check the power switch under the dust bin first, then confirm the dock LED is lit and the robot's contacts are clean. A robot stored flat for months may need twenty minutes on the dock before the status ring shows anything at all.

faqs.question: The AR-1 keeps returning to the dock mid-clean. Why?
faqs.answer: Either the battery is dropping below 15 percent, which triggers a recharge-and-resume, or the bin is full and the robot has paused. A pack that reaches 15 percent within twenty minutes of a full charge is worn and should be replaced with NW-BATT-32.

faqs.question: The AR-1 leaves streaks when mopping.
faqs.answer: Streaks come from a dry or dirty pad. Rinse the mop pad, refit it wet, and check the 180 ml water tank is seated. Mopping is an AR-1 Pro feature; the base AR-1 has no water tank.

faqs.question: The map disappeared after a firmware update.
faqs.answer: Maps are stored on the robot and are kept across updates, but an interrupted update clears them. Run one full clean to rebuild the map, then re-add zones. Do not power-cycle the dock while the status ring is pulsing blue.

faqs.question: The AR-1 smells burnt.
faqs.answer: Stop using it. A burnt smell usually means hair is wrapped tight on the roller axle and the motor is overheating, or a belt is slipping. Clear the roller and inspect it. If the smell persists or the battery pack is swollen, do not charge the robot and contact support.

faqs.question: How do I stop the AR-1 from entering one room?
faqs.answer: Add a no-go zone over the doorway in the app, or close the door. No-go zones are stored on the robot and are enforced even when the phone is off.
